newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - products dip, CFDs climb.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - products dip, CFDs climb.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Tuesday morning but dealers said the market was slow to re-start after Monday's public holiday in the UK.
Brent crude CFDs was showing some signs of strength but oil products were again slipping lower with most easing about 50 cents a tonne.
Heavy fuel swaps traded at $83.25 for May barges soon after the open compared to $83.75 and $84 on Friday.

Low sulphur was also under pressure with talk just under $87 for May, after trading in the range $87 to $87.50 on Friday. Dealers said the threat of growing Russian exports and sluggish demand in Europe was continuing to undermine confidence in May and June swaps.
"Short term it still looks bearish but in the medium term I'm bullish," said a trader.
He expected growing Asian demand to more than offset the impact of Russian exports.
Gas oil futures were down $1.25 a tonne, extending losses of $5.50 a tonne last Friday.
In northwest Europe EN590 swaps for May were unchanged around $12.50 a tonne above the screen but 0.2 percent sulphur slipped to just $3.75 above the screen.
Gas oil crack spreads were showing signs of weakness on the screen but over-the-counter swaps held close to Friday's levels of $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.80(4Q97), $4.65 (1Q8) and $4.10 (2Q98).
Jet premiums were stable after losing ground last week. The balance of may was notionally holding around $21 a tonne above the screen while June was nearer $23.50.
Gasoline was 50 cents lower with sellers asking $194.50 for May and attracting bids no better than $193.75.
June held $2 a tonne lower and crack spreads were static at last Friday levels of $4.10 a barrel and $3.10 in the third and fourth quarters respectively.
Brent CFDs were broadly stable for the balance of this week at 29 cents under June, following trade for wet Brent at just 20 cents under last Friday.
Next week and the following week both rose roughly five cents to 23 cents and 21 cents below June respectively.

Despite those gains brokers valued monthly CFDs against the IPE unchanged from Friday. The balance of May talked 32 cents under the front line Brent contract with forward levels at the following levels under the IPE: -26 cents June, -21 cents July, -17 cents 3Q97, -13 cents 4Q97. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom 171 542 4984
